scout.purpose: Hot streams exist independently of collectors, but current state and broadcast events require different replay, equality, buffering, and delivery semantics.
scout.realWorldUse: Screen UiState, repository cache state, transient signals, app-wide updates, and multiple subscribers need an intentional hot-stream contract.
scout.outcome: Expose read-only StateFlow for state, configure SharedFlow for broadcasts, and avoid event wrappers that retrigger or silently disappear.

sections.title: StateFlow always has a current value

blocks.text: StateFlow is a hot SharedFlow specialised for state. It always has a current value, replays that value to new collectors, and suppresses equal updates. MutableStateFlow.update performs atomic pure transitions; expose asStateFlow so consumers cannot mutate it. StateFlow is ideal for complete screen snapshots and observable cache state. It cannot represent completion or failure intrinsically, so encode loading and errors in the state model.

blocks.caption: Current screen state and explicitly best-effort signals expose different contracts.

sections.title: SharedFlow broadcasts under replay and buffer policy

blocks.text: SharedFlow broadcasts emissions to active subscribers. replay controls how many past values a new subscriber receives, extraBufferCapacity and overflow define slow-subscriber behaviour, and no subscribers may mean emissions disappear when replay is zero. It never completes or represents failure; materialise those signals if required. Use shareIn to turn a cold source into shared execution rather than manually forwarding it unless custom ownership is necessary.

blocks.caption: Current screen state and explicitly best-effort signals expose different contracts.

blocks.title: Events need delivery semantics
blocks.text: Replay and buffer numbers must follow a product decision about loss and duplication.

sections.title: Events require a delivery contract beyond choosing an API

blocks.text: A navigation or snackbar event is not solved automatically by SharedFlow. Decide whether it may be lost while no UI is active, delivered once per collector, persisted until acknowledged, or represented as state. A payment result should usually be durable state; a replaceable toast can be best-effort. Avoid SingleLiveEvent-style hidden consumption flags inside UiState. Test collector arrival, recreation, multiple collectors, slow handling, and no-subscriber emission.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

blocks.title: Do not use SharedFlow as durable work queue
blocks.text: With no active collector, non-replayed emissions can disappear.

inspect.title: Make the payment result durable
inspect.code:
val result = MutableSharedFlow<PaymentResult>(replay = 0)
suspend fun complete() { result.emit(PaymentResult.Success) }
walkthrough: With no active collector and no replay, the success can disappear.
Payment completion must remain observable after recreation or temporary inactivity.
Persist the transaction state and expose it through StateFlow or durable storage.
inspect.expectedOutput: Returning to the screen shows the authoritative payment outcome exactly as product policy requires.

trap_check.why: Any consumer can bypass reducer invariants and race writes.
trap_check.fix: Expose StateFlow and retain mutation in its owner.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Design a news screen with durable UiState, a best-effort scroll signal, and an acknowledged critical result, then test recreation and multiple collectors.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Every stream documents replay and loss. Critical outcomes survive absent collectors. External code cannot mutate owner state.
